Installation study

Suspended within the room, Bloom creates a sculptural volume shaped as much by its openings as by its spheres. An interior cavity draws the room’s corner into the work, allowing the architecture to become part of the composition. The spheres are shown in the original black-to-white project palette, with the intended ceramic finishes to be developed separately. At the floor, the descending chains will pool and gather into small mounds, anchoring the suspended form through gravity.

The sculpture layout uses the exported coordinates. Room width, depth, doorway, and glazing remain visual estimates, but the wall lengths now reflect 42 inches from the sliding doors to the corner, and the full run from the corner to the doorway now reads as black tile, with the doorway moved much closer to the sculpture. The newly exported floor mounds are displayed as individual interlocking 3D chain links. Nine strands feature pooling (six 18-link and three 36-link mounds). The room geometry remains a visual estimate, not a measured architectural model.

Standalone offline WebGL 2 viewer with the native Suspended Builder GLB geometry embedded. The lightweight canvas fallback does not display true chain-link geometry. Placement remains exploratory; verify floor clearances and anchor locations before installation.
